breaks.reason: Switched to ICMM water accounting; 2015-2016 not comparable (Victor 3,020 → 32,907 ML).
Namdeb and Debswana excluded from boundary (~20% of 2017 withdrawal, 99% of seawater).
Updated ICMM guidance: rainfall/run-off captured but not used now counted; surface withdrawal 28,710 → 68,060 ML.
Escondida no longer classed as water-stressed; stressed withdrawal 246,700 → 29,710 ML.
Rainwater harvested now counted; consumption flips from negative to positive.
Batu Hijau divested (≈272 GL seawater in 2015).
Goldcorp sites added, Nevada moved to joint venture; 2015-2018 not restated.
Reporting format changed (mine dewatering, precipitation, external sources).
Tahoe Resources acquisition adds Timmins, Shahuindo, La Arena.
Lihir seawater was misclassified as higher-quality water before FY19.

breaks.reason: Petrov Lake reclassified as not fresh; pit dewatering apparently excluded from discharge.

FY2022 covers only 9 months (Oct 2021 – Jun 2022) after the Sandfire acquisition.

observations.text: Site data (Water Management, Materials sheets) is for 2019 only (no year header in those sheets; Global AEM column equals the 2019 column of the Performance Summary). Corporate 5-year series 2015-2019 comes from the Performance Summary sheet.
Corporate withdrawal rose from 6116 ML (2016) to 9532 ML (2019) (+30% vs 2018); withdrawal intensity rose from 0.37 (2018) to 0.49 m3/t (2019).

Discharge (17408 ML in 2019) far exceeds withdrawal (9532 ML): likely because dewatering/contact water and site runoff are discharged without being counted as withdrawal (not explained in the file). Meadowbank alone discharged 7590 ML vs 2281 ML withdrawn. 2019 corporate discharge jumped +78% vs 2018.

Inconsistency: Meadowbank discharge 'Destination' text (H28) lists Second Portage Lake 39,700,000 m3, Whale Tail South 6,924,848 m3, Mammoth Lake 6,290,000 m3 and Nemo Lake watershed tundra 8,360,000 m3 - far more than the 7,589,601 m3 reported as discharge (H26); the text volumes are probably cumulative/lake-dewatering or design volumes. Not recorded as records.

'Total Water Used' (reported under GRI 303-5 Water Consumption) is withdrawal + recycled, not consumption; no true consumption figure (evaporation/entrainment or withdrawal-discharge) is disclosed. Recorded as other:water_used_total. Discharge is only disclosed as 'to fresh water bodies' at site level (recorded as discharge_surface); Performance Summary gives 'Total Water Discharged' (discharge_total) with identical 2019 value.

Water stress: only La India (Mexico) is in a High/Extremely High baseline water stress area (G16 = 100%); corporate share 9.64% of withdrawal (B16) - consistent with La India's withdrawal share. No absolute withdrawal_water_stressed volume is stated.
Reuse: corporate recycled share fell from 71% (2017) to 62% (2019). La India recycles only 2.7% and Meadowbank 21.1%.

Labels: withdrawal is labelled 'Total Freshwater Withdrawal' at site level but 'Total Water Withdrawn' in the summary (same values); recorded as both withdrawal_total and withdrawal_fresh for the site table.
Gold 2019: Performance Summary C10 = 1447547.407287 oz vs Materials sheet B10 = 1447551 oz (minor internal inconsistency, both recorded).

Compliance: SASB EM-MM-140a.2 (GRI & SASB Index E136) states zero significant fines/non-monetary sanctions for non-compliance with water quality permits in 2019 (recorded as water_incidents_count 0). Performance Summary: 0 significant spills in 2019 (2 in 2016 with 30,000,000 L; 2 in 2015); environmental fines 2 in 2017 totalling CAD 53,970 (not water-specific).

Discharge treatment/destination: LaRonde -> Dormenan Creek (chemical/biological), Goldex -> small creek (passive treatment), Kittila -> River Seurujoki, Pinos Altos -> La Bateria and Concheño stream, Meliadine -> Meliadine Lake (Actiflo + saline water treatment); LaRonde, Kittila and Meadowbank discharges flagged as significantly affecting water bodies (row 29).
Cyanide: LaRonde reported 4 cyanide incidents requiring regulatory reporting in 2019 (Environmental Stewardship C42); no cyanide releases off site requiring remediation.
REPORTING-YEAR OFFSET: file year = CDP submission year; each response reports the prior calendar year (2016 file -> 2015 data, 2017 -> 2016, 2018 -> 2017, 2019 -> 2018, 2020 -> 2019).

FACILITY DEFINITION: W5 "facilities" are mostly river-basin/catchment groupings of many sites (e.g. Limpopo WMA = 26 sites in 2016, 15 in 2017, 16 in 2018, 7 in 2019), so group membership changes year to year; only Los Bronces (2015, 2018-2019), Minas-Rio, Quellaveco, Victor, Unki are single sites. Site names in this file carry the catchment label; see record notes for constituents.

GROUPING CHANGES: Los Bronces was its own facility in 2015 (basin "Salado"), merged into the Aconcagua group in 2016-2017 (36,374 and 34,968 ML), and split out again under "Maipo" from 2018. Sishen/Kolomela were in the Orange WMA group in 2015 and in the Vaal group from 2016. Namibia group basin labelled "Orange" in 2015 and "South Atlantic Coast" later; De Beers Canada labelled "St. Lawrence" in 2015.

METHODOLOGY BREAK 2017: from reporting year 2017 Anglo American aligned with ICMM water accounting; group withdrawals jumped from 226,509 ML (2016) to 306,275 ML (2017) while described as "about the same"; groundwater 83,098 -> 139,176 ML; Victor facility 3,020 -> 32,907 ML. 2015-2016 values are not comparable with 2017+.

SCOPE CHANGE 2018: Namdeb and Debswana (non-managed JVs) excluded from the 2018 boundary; they were ~20% of 2017 withdrawals, 21% of discharges, 99% of seawater withdrawal (seawater 33,935 -> 15 ML). New Vaal, New Denmark, Kriel divested Feb 2018.

RESTATEMENT: the 2017 response says 2016 discharge (136,039 ML) was 3% lower than RESTATED 2015 discharge; originally reported 2015 discharge was 110,937 ML, implying a material upward restatement (~140,000 ML) that is not disclosed numerically.

CONSUMPTION DEFINITION: 2015 consumption (222,866 ML; 221,000 ML in W8.1a of the same file) far exceeds withdrawals minus discharge (137,536 ML) - it appears to be "new water consumption" incl. other definitions. From 2017 onwards consumption = withdrawals minus discharge (company acknowledges this is not a true ICMM consumption figure).

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES (facility level): 2016 data - Aconcagua (36,374) and Minas-Rio (17,251) consumption equal their withdrawals despite 248 and 13,900 ML discharged; Limpopo consumption 34,804 > withdrawal 34,260. 2015 data - several facilities have consumption > withdrawal (e.g. Debswana 25,221 vs 19,317; Limpopo 37,655 vs 37,041). 2019 data - Mackenzie facility consumption -358 ML (discharge > withdrawal). 2019 Los Bronces labelled "Much higher" although withdrawals fell 24,879 -> 16,703 ML.

RECYCLING RATE: 2015 stated as 69% (W1.1) and 64% (W8.1b) in same file; 2016 66%; 2017 ~60% (estimated); 2018 ~70%; 2019 ~70%. Company notes recycled data partly estimated because many sites lacked water balances (only 60% of sites had completed/restated water balances at end-2018). 2020 response gives "% of target achieved" 80 while text says 93%.

TARGET EVOLUTION: 2016 file - reduce consumption 14% (29,995 ML) vs 2020 BAU forecast 192,272 ML (set 2011; 16% saving achieved by 2015). 2017 file - target reset to 19% (20,595 ML) vs BAU 108,393 ML on 7 material sites, 2015 baseline (22,865 ML avoided in 2016); recycling goal changed from 80% (no date) to 75% by 2020; new goal -20% absolute freshwater intake by 2020. 2018 file - WETT replaced by Sustainable Mining Plan: 75% recycling by 2020, -20% freshwater intake by 2020 (2015 baseline), >85% recycling by 2030, -50% freshwater abstraction in water-scarce regions by 2030, no Level 3+ incidents by 2020.

TARGET PROGRESS REGRESSION: freshwater intake reduction vs 2015 reported as 13% in both the 2018 and 2019 responses (identical, possibly not updated), then 7% in the 2020 response (RY2019) - i.e. 35% of the 2020 target and 14% of the 2030 goal; company states improved water accounting puts 2020 milestones at risk and baseline will be reset in 2020 with ICMM definitions.

WATER STRESS EXPOSURE: share of operations/mines in water-stressed/high-risk areas stated as >70% (2016 file), ~75% (2017 file), 50% (2018, 2019 files), "over 50%" (2020 file). Share of withdrawals from stressed areas: 55% (2017), 58% (2018), 51-75% range "higher" (2019). All 13 facilities flagged as in water-stressed areas in 2019 except the two Canadian ones.

LOS BRONCES DROUGHT (key physical risk): 2015 - 6th consecutive dry year, ~18,000 t copper lost, ~$90.5m loss; 2017 - flooding of pit/haul roads after wet 2016-17, 2 weeks lost production, $53m; 2019 - driest year of decade-long mega-drought, production -9% to 335,000 t (2018: 369,500 t), $207m lost revenue (34,500 t x $6,000/t). Response spend: $180m recycling system (2016 file), $74m (2017 file), $70m (2018 file), $20m (2019 file), $17m (2020 file). Evaporation covers piloted (up to 85-90% evaporation reduction); CPR potential saving ~$18m/yr; evaporation-loss saving ~$15m/yr (site uses ~30 million m3/yr new fresh water at ~$2/m3).

MINAS-RIO: Peixe river supplies up to 80% of fresh water; abstraction halted Sept-Oct 2015, 16 Jul-15 Nov 2016, 24 Jul-1 Nov 2017 (regional scarcity permit limits; tailings-dam reserve nearly exhausted in 2017). March 2018 slurry pipeline leaks (318 t and 174 t into Santo Antonio stream) -> 280 days suspension, $0.6bn EBITDA impact, fines $32.4m + $17.5m (total $50m, 11 fines). One-day lost production valued at $3.8m (2018 file), $0.9m (2019 file), $6.3m (2020 file).

MOGALAKWENA / LIMPOPO: value of one day of lost production $3.3m (2018 file, revenue $1.2bn), $3.6m (2019 file, $1.3bn), $4.1m (2020 file, $1.5bn). $6m Polokwane sewage works upgrade for +6 ML/day (spent $3.8m by 2017, $5.2m by 2018, $6.7m since 2014 by 2019); treated effluent allocation raised to 20 ML/day in 2019. Regional Limpopo water balance: region extremely water stressed until beyond 2028; significant supply shortfalls expected 2022; province severely stressed 2022-2025.

OTHER RISK FIGURES: eMalahleni water reclamation plant (treats up to 50 ML/day) capex $1.5bn cited as Olifants risk magnitude (2018-2020 files). Canada (Snap Lake, Trend, Victor) water management cost ~$100m/yr (2016-2018 files) but $10m/yr in 2019 file; Trend Se treatment potential $100m (2018 file) vs $10m (2019 file). Los Bronces Donoso acid drainage: ~$30m collection system spent; treatment plant $60m (2017-2018 files) revised to $35m (2019-2020 files), only needed 2020-2022. El Soldado sulphate seepage: potential fine $6m, $1m drains. Group-wide pipeline asset review $10m after 823 m3 Los Bronces release (2017). $440m spent on a water supply project in Peru (2018 file, W7.1). Substantive-impact threshold: >$25m.

FINES/INCIDENTS: 2015 one enforcement order (Minas-Rio, $0); 2016 two Minas-Rio fines ($32,375 and $274,445); 2017 no water fines reported; 2018 11 fines $50m (Minas-Rio); 2019 2 administrative fines $54,000 (Brazil, contested). Level 3 environmental incidents: 14 (2014), 6 (2015), 4 (2016), 2 (2017), 5 + one Level 4 (2018, stricter classification), 1 (2019). Coal SA had two mine-water overflow incidents at Khwezela/Landau in 2016 (Kopseer, Schoongezicht dams).

CAPEX/OPEX TRENDS (estimated % change in water-related spend): 2015 capex +13%/opex -4% (Platinum & Kumba only); 2016 +24%/+27%; 2017 +10%/+10% (forward capex +500%); 2018 -50%/-50% (forward +50%/+10%); 2019 +10%/+10% (forward capex +100%). Company states it has no clear definition of water capex. >$10m invested to close gaps vs new water standard (2018 file).

CLIMATE/FORESIGHT: climate vulnerability studies (Imperial College, UK Met Office, CSIR) rank Chile and Peru as highest-risk; Mogalakwena modelling predicts ~10% increase in high/low rainfall margins, shorter wetter rainy periods, longer dry periods; Platinum SA statistical climate signal expected beyond 2048; company cites predicted 40% global water shortfall by 2030. Waterless-mine ambition: dry processing/CPR expected to allow 80% process-water reuse and 30-40% less water per unit of production.

DATA QUALITY: water withdrawals and consumption externally verified (76-100% of facilities; ISAE 3000 cited in the 2017 response) in the 2016 and 2017 responses, but "Not verified" for all aspects in the 2018 response; 2019-2020 responses repeatedly state data "has not been verified or validated against the water balance".

COMMUNITY WATER SPEND: $1.72m community water & sanitation projects in 2015; $5.3m CSI water & sanitation in 2016; Mogalakwena supplied ~35,000 residents in 12 villages by bowser (2015); Mapela community water project targeting 70,000 people (45,000 connected by 2018).

FACILITY vs GROUP TOTALS: sum of W5 facility withdrawals is below group total each year (2015: 246,598 vs 248,473; 2016: 226,340 vs 226,509; 2017: 296,887 vs 306,275; 2018: 217,288 vs 227,497; 2019: 208,989 vs 209,868 ML) - group totals include offices, exploration, labs, Element Six, Vergelegen etc. Sum of 2015 facility discharges (102,498) is well below the 110,937 group total.

PRODUCTION VALUE fields in W4.1c (e.g. Limpopo 28,483,061 in 2018 file; stated as tonnes milled/processed in 2019-2020 files) were not extracted as ore_processed_t because the unit is only implied and basins are aggregated.
Single reporting year (2019). The Water sheet has no year header; year taken from file name and GRI index (all references are to 2019 reports). Units: ML (cell A3).

Data compiled per ICMM Water Accounting Framework (GRI index J68-J70). Withdrawal/discharge/consumption split into High Quality and Low Quality; source-level components (rivers/streams, external storages, aquifer interception, bore fields, entrainment, municipal, waste water) are recorded under other:*_hq / other:*_lq keys and NOT summed into withdrawal_surface/withdrawal_ground (summing would be a computed value).

Water-stressed operations (row 6, 'Operations in water stressed areas'): withdrawal 36027.8 ML of 181516.9 ML total. This row equals the sum of the '*'-marked sites (Jabal Sayid, Pierina, and the five Nevada Gold Mines sites Carlin, Cortez, Long Canyon, Phoenix, Turquoise Ridge), which are exactly the sites with Baseline catchment stress '4. High' or '5. Very high' (col BK). Site-level withdrawal_water_stressed was not recorded separately.
Recycled/reused water (501129 ML) is ~2.8x total withdrawal; reuse efficiency (AX4) 73.4%.
Total change in storage is negative (U4 = -37478.8 ML), driven by Pueblo Viejo (U31 -20301.7) and Nevada Gold Mines (U54 -18373.1), i.e. stored water decreased in 2019.
Several intensity cells (AY-BB) on closure sites hold #DIV/0! errors (cached value 7); these were skipped.

Withdrawal intensity per ounce (AY4 = 0.0213 ML/oz) does not reconcile with Total Withdrawal / Ounces of Gold Produced (T4/BC4 = 0.0241); the per-tonne intensity (AZ4) does reconcile with T4/BE4. The per-ounce denominator is likely gold-equivalent ounces - treat per-oz intensities with caution.

Production in the Water sheet (gold 7526000 oz, copper 370000000 lb) differs from GRI index 102-7 (J12: attributable 5.465 Moz gold, 432 Mlb copper). Water-sheet figures appear to be 100%-basis for operated sites; copper only covers Lumwana + Jabal Sayid (Zaldivar is not in the water data).

Nevada Gold Mines (JV formed 1 July 2019, 61.5% Barrick) is reported as a subtotal row (54) with sites Carlin, Cortez, Long Canyon, Phoenix, Turquoise Ridge; only the individual sites were recorded. Carlin reports storage change -12,459.8 ML and 27,648 ML consumption against 15,188 ML withdrawal. Cortez shows only aquifer-interception withdrawal and no discharge.

Country/region subtotal rows (Mali, Africa and Middle East, Latin America and Asia Pacific, North America, etc.) and row 5 'Operations' (excluding closure sites) were not recorded; '_corporate' uses row 4 'Barrick'. Site withdrawal_total values sum exactly to T4.
Porgera (PNG) has zero consumption-by-evaporation but 26,836 ML Low Quality surface discharge (AE36) - nearly all of its 29,431 ML withdrawal - and 2,595 ML 'other' consumption.

Water non-compliances (sheet 'Incidents and Spills' col G): 19 in total (G3) - Kibali 8, Porgera 7, Cortez 2, Lagunas Norte 1, Hemlo 1. Total environment-related fines count L3 = 0, but 'Value of environmental-related fines' M3 = 18 (no currency; value attributed to Kibali/DRC M10) - not water-specific, so not recorded as water_fines_usd.
No targets or multi-year trend data in this workbook.
Fiscal year basis: all BHP values are for financial years ending 30 June (FY2023 = 1 Jul 2022 - 30 Jun 2023); year field = FY end year.

Site-level (operated asset) water data is only provided for FY2023; FY2019-FY2023 is corporate-only. Data excludes OZ Minerals (acquired FY2023) and discontinued operations (BHP Mitsui Coal, Petroleum). Values rounded to nearest 10 ML.

Water-stress classification change: withdrawals in water stress areas were 233,190 ML (FY2021) and 246,700 ML (FY2022) but only 29,710 ML in FY2023 (Environment!E19:G19). In FY2023 only Legacy assets and Pampa Norte are flagged as in water stress (Water!E7, I7); Escondida (226,190 ML, largely seawater) is no longer flagged, so the drop is a classification/scope change, not a real reduction. Same pattern for discharge (123,200 -> 2,630 ML) and consumption (115,400 -> 33,710 ML) in stress areas.

Methodology change (footnotes Environment!A60 / Water!A119): FY2019-FY2021 withdrawals include only rainfall/run-off captured AND used in-year; from FY2022 (updated ICMM guidance) captured-but-not-used rainfall/run-off is also included. FY2022+ withdrawals and surface-water withdrawals are therefore not comparable with earlier years (surface water jumps 28,710 -> 68,060 ML FY2021->FY2022; Type 2 withdrawals 35,430 -> 67,120 ML).
Other managed water was reported as "diversions" before FY2022; from FY2022 it is broken down by quality type (Environment!A62).

Restatement flag: the Environment and Water sheets state that italic data has been restated since the ESG Standards and Databook 2022. Essentially all FY2019-FY2022 cells on the Environment sheet (and the prior-year rows of the Water 5-year tables) are italic-formatted, so the file does not allow isolating which specific values were restated; records carry a note where the cell is italic.

Nickel West Kwinana withdrawal-by-source was restated for FY2017-FY2019 using site-specific Water Corporation source proportions; from FY2021 all Kwinana supply is reported as third-party (Water!A121). Third-party withdrawals are blank ("-") for FY2019-FY2020 in both the Environment sheet and the Water sheet (H48:H49).

Water quality typing: BHP uses Type 1/2/3 (MCA Water Accounting Framework). Per schema, Type 1 is mapped to withdrawal_fresh; Type 2 and Type 3 are kept as other:withdrawal_type2/type3 (no single stated low-quality total). Note Water!C44 labels Type 2 "High Quality", so under ICMM 2021 conventions high-quality = Type 1 + Type 2.

BMA recycled/reused uses a non-ICMM method (volume returned from operational tasks to water stores) due to climatic variation (Water!A116). Corporate recycled/reused jumped from 260,900 ML (FY2022) to 344,710 ML (FY2023); Pampa Norte alone reports 262,750 ML reused in FY2023 (Water!I31), ~9x its 28,640 ML withdrawal.

Escondida dominates: 226,190 of 408,540 ML FY2023 withdrawals (55%), 213,920 ML of it seawater (desalination) and zero Type 1 water; 121,630 ML discharged to sea. Nickel West consumption (16,870 ML) exceeds withdrawal (16,160 ML), with 16,160 ML "consumption - other".
Consumption FY2020 is stated as 251,969.8 ML (Environment!D29), the only unrounded value in the series. Some cells are text with embedded spaces ("43, 450" in Environment!D15) - parsed as 43,450.

Production is only available as copper-equivalent production (kt Cu-eq) per asset for FY2020-FY2023 in the GHG emissions by asset sheet (recorded as other_production in t Cu-eq); no ore processed or metal production figures in this databook.

FY2023 significant environmental fines: 5 in Australia (all BMA, US$47,503; effluent, tailings and mine-affected-water releases) and 3 in Chile (Escondida, US$6,779; Laguna Seca ponds, groundwater extraction monitoring, air quality). Accidental discharges of water and tailings reported as 0 ML every year FY2019-FY2023 (excludes Samarco dam failure).

Targets: BHP committed to publish context-based water targets (CBWTs) in FY2023, applicable to FY2030, with progress reporting from FY2024 (Social value scorecard!A19/B19). No numeric water target is given in this file.

Water stress is defined via WWF Water Risk Filter (high/very high physical risk) per CEO Water Mandate; SASB EM-MM-140a.1 (WRI Aqueduct basis) is only cross-referenced to bhp.com, not reported in the file.

Duplicated tables (Water!B vs Environment!G, Water 5-year tables rows 45-58, "Water data by asset" sheet) were cross-checked and not recorded twice; they agree except: BHP discharge table Water!B54: Water!B54="–" vs Environment!G21=0 | BHP discharge table Water!B55: Water!B55="–" vs Environment!F21=0 | BHP discharge table Water!B56: Water!B56="–" vs Environment!E21=0 | BHP discharge table Water!B57: Water!B57="–" vs Environment!D21=0 | BHP discharge table Water!B58: Water!B58="–" vs Environment!C21=0 (Type 1 discharge shown as a dash vs 0).

Kumtor and Mount Milligan both show 0% of withdrawal from High/Extremely High baseline water stress in 2019 (Table 8 p.32); Öksüt shows 100%. waterStressReported left null for 0% sites because the report does not classify them as low stress.
Öksüt was under construction in 2019 (commercial production 2020); 2019 is the first year water data reported for it (2019 report p.32). Status left null.

Reclassification: 2019 ESG report fn 8 (p.32) states Kumtor's main source Petrov Lake is not fresh water under SASB/GRI (>1000 ppm TDS) although previous reports presented it as such; Kumtor 2019 fresh withdrawal therefore reported as 0 and 7.86 Mm3 as 'other water'.

Terminology inconsistency: 2019 report text (p.32) calls 7.86 Mm3 (Kumtor) and 7.59 Mm3 (Mount Milligan) 'water consumption', but in Table 8 those are withdrawals; Table 8 consumption for Kumtor is only 1.72 Mm3. Mount Milligan 2018 Data Supplement likewise labels total withdrawal as 'Total water consumption' (defined as all water withdrawn). These were mapped to withdrawal_total.

Mount Milligan 2019 Table 8 shows both 7.59 Mm3 freshwater and 4.44 Mm3 other water withdrawn (and consumed, with 0 discharge), while the text gives 7.59 Mm3 as total 2019 water use; the 4.44 figure is unexplained.

Kumtor 2018 'water consumption' of 7.46 Mm3 in the 2019 report (p.32) cannot be reconciled with the 2018 Data Supplement (Petrov Lake 5.17 + pit water to mill 1.54 = 6.71 Mm3; total pit pumping 27.45 Mm3).

Kumtor pit dewatering 'pumped to the environment' was 12.75/29.24/25.17 Mm3 (2016/2017/2018, 2018 Supplement p.13) but 2019 Table 8 reports total Kumtor discharge of only 6.13 Mm3, suggesting pit dewatering is excluded from the 2019 discharge definition (scope change).
Kumtor 2018 note (p.13): pit pumping total 27.45 Mm3 does not equal table rows to mill (1.54) + to environment (25.17) = 26.71 Mm3.

Mount Milligan 2018 water figures were revised following a 2019 methodology review (2018 Supplement p.14 note 9), lowering the recycled-water ratio (75.7% in 2018 vs 87.8% 2017, 86.6% 2016). Note 9 defines 'water recycled and reused' as demand minus consumption, though the text wording reverses the subtraction.
Mount Milligan ratio row in 2018 Supplement Table 8 is labelled 'mil.m³' but is a percentage. Kumtor 'Ore Feed to Mill' is labelled 'tonnes' but values (6.3, 6.2, 6.3) are million tonnes.

Water scarcity at Mount Milligan: low water storage from 2016 caused processing shutdown Dec 2017 to early 2018; an EA Certificate amendment allowed limited withdrawal from Philip Lake until Oct 2018 (2018 Supplement p.8); surface pumping from Philip Lake 1 and Rainbow Creek authorized to Nov 2021, groundwater licences (Meadows Creek, Lower Rainbow wellfields) to Dec 2023; long-term groundwater not proven over life-of-mine (2019 report p.32).

Rainwater/snowpack share at Mount Milligan fell from 6.2 Mm3 (2016) to 2.83 Mm3 (2018) while groundwater rose from 0.056 to 2.95 Mm3 and surface water from 0 to 1.64 Mm3 (2018 Supplement p.14): shift to active abstraction during drought.

2019 incident/fine: Kumtor received a penalty for discharging without permits and exceeding maximum allowable concentration (MAC) standards from its Effluent and Sewage Treatment Plants; stated as resolved and not significant; amount not disclosed (2019 report p.32). 1 water non-compliance at Kumtor, 0 at Mount Milligan and Öksüt (Table 9).

Mount Milligan and Öksüt are designed as zero-discharge facilities (2019 report p.29-30). About 97% of Kumtor water is used at the mill and ~5 Mm3 is recycled within the mill annually (p.30, approximate, not recorded as a record).

Chart labelling inconsistency: the p.57 chart labels the bars 2018-2021, but the values match the p.76 table periods 2019-2020 to 2021-2022 (i.e. labels appear shifted by one year / use the period start year).

Sotiel mine reports zero fresh water intake in all three periods but discharges 57-132 thousand m3; Aguas Teñidas reports zero discharge in 2021-2022 (vs 133,676 m3 in 2020-2021). Discharge rose sharply in 2020-2021 (530,234 m3) then fell to 133,685 m3 in the 9-month 2021-2022 period.

Ore processed tonnage is not stated in the document (only ratios per tonne and the plant capacity of >4.5 Mt/yr, p.78); ore_processed_t therefore not recorded. Production is given only as concentrate tonnage (copper, zinc, lead) on p.79, not contained metal.
Methodology: water footprint calculated per Water Footprint Network standard and MATSA is starting adaptation to ISO 14046 water footprint (p.58). Member of EsAgua network (Gold category) (p.57).

Targets/initiatives: LIFE Remine Water project (zero liquid discharge treatment train) targets recovery of 90% of water for reuse, 90% of sulphuric acid, 70% of copper and 40% of zinc from effluents, and 70% lower CO2 vs thermal evaporation (pp.59-60). Effluent concentrations to the exterior reportedly reduced since 2017 (grey water footprint) (p.59). No quantified corporate water withdrawal target.
Compliance: no non-compliances with applicable environmental regulations detected and no sanctions received from the competent authorities (p.53, GRI 307-1).

Site-level water data is 2022 only (9 operated sites: 4 Elk Valley coal mines, Highland Valley Copper, Red Dog, Carmen de Andacollo, Quebrada Blanca, Trail smelter). Corporate (all operations) and mining-operations totals cover 2016-2022; quality/source breakdowns cover 2021-2022. Non-operated Antamina and closed sites (Cardinal River, Coal Mountain, Pend Oreille) have no water data in this file.

Trail Operations (smelter, not a mine) accounts for 69,626 of 117,327 ML (59%) of 2022 withdrawals, almost entirely high-quality surface water (68,232 ML, T97); "Mining Operations" totals exclude Trail (47,701 ML).

Water-stressed areas: only Carmen de Andacollo and Quebrada Blanca (Chile) are classified as water-stressed (WRI Aqueduct); 25% of sites. Water-stressed withdrawal 12,639 ML in 2022 vs 12,580.6 ML in 2021, 99% high-quality water (mostly groundwater at CdA).

Other managed water (184,327 ML in 2022, all at mining operations and mostly Elk Valley coal: Fording River 82,808, Elkview 44,262) exceeds operational withdrawals and drives total discharge (235,671 ML); discharge > withdrawal is therefore expected for Teck.

Consumption exceeds withdrawal at Highland Valley Copper (24,212 vs 17,180 ML) and Quebrada Blanca (2,305 vs 2,139 ML) in 2022, consistent with drawdown of stored water; corporate change of storage is 13,079 ML (2022) and 9,107.7 ML (2021).

Trend (all operations): withdrawal 117,931 ML (2016) -> 128,146 (2018 peak) -> 117,327 (2022); consumption fell from 62,033 ML (2018) to 52,904 ML (2022); reuse/recycle volume fell from 176,563 ML (2017) to 134,131 ML (2022) and the reuse rate from 80% (2017) to 74% (2022).

Terminology change: "water withdrawal" was previously "water withdrawal for use"/"new water use"; "other managed water" was previously "water withdrawal discharged without use"; "operational water use" was previously "total water use". Surface water includes precipitation/runoff not diverted around operations, so there is no separate rain/runoff source.

Reuse rate cells (row 27 / row 77) store fractions displayed as % (0.74 = 74%); converted to percent. Intensities are m3 per tonne of ore or raw coal processed (operational water use intensity, row 78) and m3 of new water per tonne processed (row 79, recorded as water_intensity_reported); Quebrada Blanca and Trail intensities are "N/A". The Teck-level intensity is on a mining-operations basis.
